category.name: Lists
category.preferred_workflow: Create a List via doc.Lists.Add(ListTemplate), assign it to DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.List, set ListFormat.ListLevelNumber for each desired nesting level, write the paragraph content, and finally call ListFormat.RemoveNumbers to terminate the list before adding non-list content.

strict_api_bans: Do not reference APIs that are not present in Aspose.Words 26.10.0, such as ListFormat.IncreaseIndent, ListFormat.DecreaseIndent, ListNumberStyle, or ListLevel.StartingNumber.
Do not omit the assignment of builder.ListFormat.List before writing list items.
canonical_patterns: Create a list with doc.Lists.Add(ListTemplate) and store the returned List object.
Apply the list to the builder by setting builder.ListFormat.List, then control nesting with builder.ListFormat.ListLevelNumber.
Terminate list formatting with builder.ListFormat.RemoveNumbers once the list sequence is complete.
nullable_warning_prevention: Guard any List or ListLevel reference with a null check before accessing its members.
Validate that a Paragraph node is not null before reading or writing its ListFormat properties.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Use of removed or renamed list APIs
common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation fails with CS1061 because ListFormat does not contain IncreaseIndent, DecreaseIndent, or ListNumberStyle members.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code references API members that were removed or renamed in the current Aspose.Words version.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Replace the missing members with supported alternatives: control nesting via ListFormat.ListLevelNumber and use NumberStyle enum values such as NumberStyle.Bullet or NumberStyle.UppercaseRoman.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Consult the Aspose.Words 26.10.0 documentation for the exact member names before writing list-related code.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation fails with CS1061 for ListLevel.StartingNumber, ListLevel.Indentation, or ListLevel.BulletChar.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Older property names were used; the current API uses ListLevel.StartAt for the starting number, ListLevel.NumberPosition/TextPosition for indentation, and NumberFormat for custom bullet characters.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Use ListLevel.StartAt to set the initial number, adjust ListLevel.NumberPosition and ListLevel.TextPosition for indentation, and set ListLevel.NumberFormat to a custom character string.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Reference the ListLevel class in the official API reference to ensure property names are up-to-date.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Missing list assignment before writing items
common_failure_patterns.symptom: Paragraphs are added but appear as plain text without list numbering or bullets.
common_failure_patterns.cause: builder.ListFormat.List was never set, so the builder does not know which list to apply.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Assign the List object to builder.ListFormat.List immediately before writing the first list paragraph.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Always set builder.ListFormat.List as the first step of any list-creation workflow.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Subsequent paragraphs unintentionally continue the previous list style.
common_failure_patterns.cause: builder.ListFormat.RemoveNumbers was not called after the list sequence.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Invoke builder.ListFormat.RemoveNumbers right after the last list item and before adding non-list content.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Include a RemoveNumbers call in every list workflow to reset the builder's list state.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation fails with CS1061 because CompatibilityOptions or Document does not expose an OoxmlCompliance property.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The property was removed from the API; compliance is now controlled via SaveOptions.
common_failure_patterns.fix: When saving, create a DocxSaveOptions instance and set its Compliance property to OoxmlCompliance.Iso29500_2008_Strict (or a later enum value).
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Use SaveOptions to configure compliance settings instead of accessing non-existent Document members.

examples.task: Create a default numbered list in a Word document using DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.ApplyNumberDefault method.
Apply a default bulleted list to paragraphs with DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.ApplyBulletDefault method for formatting.
Set ListLevelNumber to three before adding a paragraph to create a third-level list item in the document.
Increase list indent programmatically using DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.IncreaseIndent to move paragraph deeper within the current list structure.
Decrease list indent with DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.DecreaseIndent to promote paragraph to higher level in the outline.
Remove numbering from a paragraph by calling DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.RemoveNumbers method to stop list formatting.
Create a custom List object, configure its levels, and add it to Document.Lists collection.
Add a new List to the document's ListCollection and assign it to multiple paragraphs to share formatting.
Assign an existing List to a paragraph by setting Paragraph.ListFormat.List property to apply the desired list style.
Clone an existing List, modify its level start values, and apply the cloned list to new sections.
Set NumberStyle of a ListLevel to UpperRoman to generate Roman numeral list items.
Apply a custom bullet character to a list by setting ListLevel.NumberStyle to Bullet and defining BulletChar.
Define StartingNumber for a ListLevel to begin numbering at five instead of default one.
Restart numbering for each new section by resetting ListLevel.StartingNumber before applying the list.
Create a numbered list that restarts numbering at each new chapter by resetting StartingNumber on chapter start.
Create a nine-level hierarchical list by defining properties for each ListLevel up to level nine.
Create a multi-level list with alternating bullet and number styles by configuring each ListLevel individually.
Adjust ListLevel indentation by setting ListLevel.Indentation to 36 points for proper alignment.
Apply a custom tab stop to list levels to align text after numbers using ListLevel.TabPosition property.
Configure TabPosition of a ListLevel to 72 points to align text after list number.
Validate that each list in a document does not exceed nine levels to comply with API constraints.
Implement error handling for attempts to create more than nine list levels, catching the resulting exception.
Ensure OoxmlCompliance is set higher than Ecma376 before saving document to retain custom list settings.
Check document OoxmlCompliance property and set to higher than Ecma376 when modifying list definitions.
Retrieve a specific List from Document.Lists by its ID and adjust its level properties programmatically.
Iterate through Document.Lists collection to modify all list definitions uniformly across the document.
Apply a uniform list style to all lists by iterating over Document.Lists and updating each level.
Programmatically increase list level depth for a paragraph using DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.IncreaseIndent within a loop.
Programmatically decrease list level depth for a paragraph using DocumentBuilder.ListFormat.DecreaseIndent inside a conditional.
Programmatically remove list formatting from selected paragraphs while preserving their indentation using ListFormat.RemoveNumbers.

narrative.overview: The Lists category for Aspose.Words demonstrates how to create, configure, and manipulate Word list structures using the DocumentBuilder and List APIs. Verified examples show correct usage of ListTemplate, ListLevel properties, and ListFormat methods to produce numbered, bulleted, and custom hierarchical lists.
narrative.purpose: Provide an AI coding assistant with concise, authoritative guidance for generating and managing Word lists in Aspose.Words, ensuring that generated code compiles against version 26.10.0 and follows best-practice patterns for list creation, nesting, formatting, and cleanup.
validation_priorities: Count Paragraph nodes where para.ListFormat.IsListItem is true to verify that the expected number of list items were generated.
maintenance_notes: Update the example code whenever a new Aspose.Words version is released to reflect any API changes and keep the documentation in sync.
